new_entities.name: Long-term nitrofurantoin use in older adults

edges.effect_quant: The clearest quantitative signal comes from a large matched cohort of older adults in which chronic nitrofurantoin exposure was associated with a higher risk of lung injury than acute exposure, with an adjusted risk ratio of 1.53 (95% CI 1.04 to 2.24).
edges.population: older adults receiving repeated or prophylactic nitrofurantoin exposure
edges.mechanism: Chronic nitrofurantoin exposure can generate reactive intermediates within pulmonary tissue, driving interstitial inflammation and, in susceptible patients, a slow fibrotic pattern rather than just an acute hypersensitivity reaction. Older age and prolonged exposure matter because the lung has more time to accumulate injury before the drug is stopped.
edges.summary: This edge is anchored on the 2016 matched cohort from a large integrated health system, which showed that long-term nitrofurantoin use in older adults carries a higher risk of clinically recognized lung injury than short-course use. Later mechanistic and clinical reviews do not overturn that finding; they mainly reinforce that the chronic form is uncommon but real and can evolve toward interstitial fibrosis if it is missed.
edges.caveats: The absolute event rate is low, and most older adults on nitrofurantoin will never develop pulmonary fibrosis. But when nitrofurantoin is used as long-term prophylaxis, new cough or dyspnea should not be waved away because the chronic toxicity pattern can be subtle at onset and more consequential than the typical acute course.

evidence.citation: SantosJM et al 2016 J Am Geriatr Soc
evidence.notes: Evaluation of the Risk of Nitrofurantoin Lung Injury and Its Efficacy in Diminished Kidney Function in Older Adults in a Large Integrated Healthcare System: A Matched Cohort Study.
